1. (Currently amended) A method comprising: a processor determining that a benefit payment is due to be made to a recipient; the processor accessing a data store containing records of payment transactions made by the recipient; the processor receiving an indication from the data store that the recipient had successfully performed a biometric user authentication with respect to at least one of the payment transactions; the processor accepting the received indication as proof-of-life with respect to the recipient; the processor verifying that the biometric user authentication was performed by the recipient using a unique biological or behavioral characteristic that is non-repeatable and device-specific; and the processor making the benefit payment to the recipient in response to said proof-of-life, wherein the benefit payment is made only after the processor has independently verified the recipient's identity through the biometric authentication data stored in the data store.

2. (Currently amended) The method of claim 1, wherein said at least one payment transaction occurred during a pre-determined period of time prior to said accessing step, and wherein the processor confirms that the biometric authentication data has not been compromised or altered since the payment transaction.

3. (Currently amended) The method of claim 2, wherein said pre-determined period of time is seven days, and wherein the processor performs a cryptographic verification of the biometric authentication record.

4. (Currently amended) The method of claim 2, wherein said pre-determined period of time is 24 hours, and wherein the processor performs a cryptographic verification of the biometric authentication record.

5. (Currently amended) The method of claim 1, wherein the benefit payment is a social insurance transfer payment, and wherein the processor is configured to prevent fraudulent benefit distributions by validating the biometric authentication against a government database.

6. (Currently amended) The method of claim 1, wherein the at least one of the payment transactions includes a credit card account transaction and/or a debit card account transaction, and wherein the processor retrieves biometric authentication metadata associated with each transaction.

7. (Currently amended) The method of claim 6, wherein a mobile device was used by the recipient to initiate the at least one payment transaction, and wherein the processor verifies that the biometric authentication was performed on the same mobile device.

8. (Currently amended) The method of claim 1, wherein the benefit payment is made via an electronic monetary transfer to an account owned by the recipient, and wherein the processor executes the transfer only after confirming the biometric proof-of-life.

9. (Currently amended) The method of claim 1, wherein the benefit payment is made by sending a check to the recipient, and wherein the processor records the biometric proof-of-life verification in an audit log prior to authorizing the check issuance.

10. (Currently amended) A method comprising: a processor determining that a benefit payment is due to be made to a recipient; the processor accessing, at a first point in time, a data store containing records of payment transactions made by the recipient; the processor determining that the data store contains an indication that the recipient had successfully performed a biometric user authentication most recently with respect to one of said payment transactions at a second point in time earlier than the first point in time; the processor comparing a time interval defined by the second and first points in time with a pre-determined permissive time interval; the processor making the benefit payment, without requiring additional proof-of-life authentication of the recipient, in a case where the time interval defined by the second and first points in time does not exceed the pre-determined permissive time interval; the processor requiring proof-of-life authentication of the recipient, prior to making the benefit payment, in a case where the time interval defined by the second and first points in time exceeds the pre-determined permissive time interval; and wherein the processor verifies that the biometric user authentication was performed using a unique biological or behavioral characteristic that is non-repeatable and device-specific.

11. (Currently amended) The method of claim 10, wherein the pre-determined permissive time interval is seven days, and wherein the processor performs a cryptographic verification of the biometric authentication record.

12. (Currently amended) The method of claim 10, wherein the pre-determined permissive time interval is 24 hours, and wherein the processor performs a cryptographic verification of the biometric authentication record.

13. (Currently amended) The method of claim 10, wherein the benefit payment is a social insurance transfer payment, and wherein the processor is configured to prevent fraudulent benefit distributions by validating the biometric authentication against a government database.

16. (Currently amended) The apparatus of claim 15, wherein said pre-determined period of time is seven days, and wherein the processor performs a cryptographic verification of the biometric authentication record.
